one_line: Shared research-to-publication workspace for humans and agents.
what_it_does: Searches and compares papers, pins sources, drafts and revises a paper, and submits it through a real publishing pipeline in shared visible state.
leverage_rationale: Structured research, drafting, and publication tools operate on the same visible workspace and consequential state; pixel-driving would be substantially less reliable.
leverage_evidence: Pitch and about text describe shared sources, draft, session, and publication state.
Agent can search archive, read reviews, pin sources, prepare/revise a paper, and publish through the real pipeline.
execution_rationale: The described end-to-end workflow is coherent and the Devpost packaging is substantial, but no submitted video frames were available as direct product-motion proof.
execution_evidence: Public repo and live demo are reported.
About text specifies a complete research-to-submission workflow and visible updates.
impact_rationale: Researchers and writers have a concrete need for traceable literature synthesis and collaborative drafting; the shared workflow plausibly reduces agent opacity.
impact_evidence: Product targets literature review and publishing.
Real moderation and five-model peer-review submission pipeline is claimed.
creativity_rationale: The visible human-agent research desk combines literature review, shared editing, and actual publication consequences in a memorable way.
creativity_evidence: Concept explicitly reframes the agent from a separate conversation into a co-present publishing workspace.
usability_note: Visible shared workspace and review-oriented flow suggest good usability; end-to-end operation is not directly observed.
red_flags: No video frame sheets submitted; end-to-end claims rely on text and packaging.
standouts: Consequential publish action remains in the same human-visible workflow.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP delta and credible research/publishing concept despite limited direct execution evidence.

one_line: Shared structured tactical mission-graph editor for designers and agents.
what_it_does: Lets humans and agents create, edit, validate, repair, and analyze a tactical mission graph through domain tools.
leverage_rationale: Agents manipulate mission-domain objects and relationships directly rather than guessing at a spatial canvas, with validation and analysis unavailable through simple clicking alone.
leverage_evidence: Devpost preview visibly shows a connected tactical graph with rooms and mission steps.
About text lists get state, create/update/delete, placement, connections, validation, and analysis tools.
execution_rationale: The mission graph is visually coherent and the stated tool surface covers the central design workflow; repair/hardening are claimed more than directly shown.
execution_evidence: Screenshot preview shows an ordered connected mission from infiltration through extraction.
Live demo and public repo are reported; 11 tools and central operations are enumerated.
impact_rationale: Level designers have a real structural-editing and validation problem, and shared graph state could make agent assistance useful in production-like workflows.
impact_evidence: Product is explicitly aimed at human designers building tactical missions.
Validation and structural hardening address concrete graph-quality needs.
creativity_rationale: Applying WebMCP to a professional-style mission graph and making structural validation part of collaboration is a fresh, ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Visible tactical graph spans rooms, entities, and routes rather than generic nodes.
Concept emphasizes repair and hardening, not only generation.
usability_note: The graph preview is legible and domain-oriented; accessibility and deeper interaction are not independently observed.
red_flags: Static packaging view does not show actual agent invocation or validation repair sequence.
standouts: Strong shared-state framing for a spatial creative editor.
advance_reason: One of the clearest cases where structured WebMCP operations materially improve agent reliability on a complex canvas.

one_line: Agent-native marketplace with structured discovery, optimization, and human-approved checkout.
what_it_does: Provides product search/filtering, collaborative cart operations, budget optimization, and a human-in-the-loop purchase flow.
leverage_rationale: Typed catalog and cart tools materially improve multi-constraint procurement and shared cart state, though a capable browser agent could eventually perform much of the same flow.
leverage_evidence: Screenshot shows 8 WebMCP tools ready, search/categories, products, cart subtotal, and savings cards.
About text enumerates structured search, specification filtering, cart, and optimization tools.
execution_rationale: The screenshot shows a coherent marketplace dashboard and product grid, but checkout and agent execution are not directly demonstrated in the submitted evidence.
execution_evidence: Visible product cards, filters, cart status, and agent controls.
Live demo and public repo are reported.
impact_rationale: Shopping and procurement users have a clear need for reliable constraint satisfaction, budget control, and safer agent-assisted checkout.
impact_evidence: Product explicitly targets multi-item budget and specification constraints.
Human-in-the-loop checkout addresses purchase-risk concerns.
creativity_rationale: The collaborative marketplace is a strong synthesis of agent shopping and human oversight, though the category and core workflow are familiar.
creativity_evidence: Visible collaborative synergy and agent savings framing.
8 standardized tools are integrated into the marketplace surface.
usability_note: Product discovery UI is clear; no direct checkout observation.
red_flags: No frame-sheet submission; screenshot is packaging plus static demo preview.
standouts: Good separation between autonomous optimization and human purchase confirmation.
advance_reason: Credible commerce workflow with a meaningful structured-agent advantage and visible product polish.

one_line: Conversational photo editor that explains each edit to beginners.
what_it_does: Applies natural-language photo edits, explains controls and values, supports per-step undo, highlighting, and histogram auditing.
leverage_rationale: The agent can operate exact editor controls while translating terminology and preserving shared history, making natural-language learning and precise reversible edits central rather than bolted on.
leverage_evidence: Frame evidence describes visible edit cards naming controls, values, explanations, and individual undo.
Transcript claims slider movement, highlighting, histogram reading, and split comparison.
execution_rationale: Video transcript and frames support a coherent workflow across editing, explanation, undo, teaching, and audit; the product is unusually complete for its scope.
execution_evidence: 138-second video transcript describes cold-to-golden-hour edit, control cards, undo, highlighting, histogram audit, and split view.
Screenshot preview shows load/start options, explanatory cards, reversibility, and local-photo messaging.
impact_rationale: Beginners with real photos and little editing vocabulary are a specific audience, and the product directly addresses both the editing and learning barriers.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets people unfamiliar with tint, saturation, and exposure.
Plain-language explanations and guided highlighting support learning without sacrificing control.
creativity_rationale: The concept makes explanation and learning part of every image edit, with the same agent able to teach, act, and audit.
creativity_evidence: Interaction model combines reversible agent editing with vocabulary instruction and self-directed learning.
56 local tools and no-server framing are pursued coherently.
usability_note: Natural language, per-edit history, undo, and visual teaching cues strongly support beginners.
standouts: Strong end-to-end evidence and unusually thoughtful beginner pedagogy.
Human retains control through per-step undo.
advance_reason: Excellent execution and a clear, meaningful WebMCP-enabled teaching/editing loop.

one_line: Accessible 2D flow editor that helps blind users verify agent changes.
what_it_does: Edits node-and-connection diagrams with accessible UI, structured tools, and deep links to evidence of changes.
leverage_rationale: Structured flow operations plus deep links to evidence address the hard verification problem more directly than screen-reader navigation or pixel-driving.
leverage_evidence: Screenshot shows a 17-node connected flow with edit controls and branching states.
About text describes create/edit/delete tools and deep links to evidence of actions.
execution_rationale: The screenshot demonstrates a substantial editor and accessible workflow representation, but does not show the agent verification sequence end-to-end.
execution_evidence: Visible Edit nodes panel, add node controls, auto layout, and connected 17-node workflow.
About text claims keyboard and screen-reader accessibility plus verification-oriented tooling.
impact_rationale: Blind users verifying complex agent-operated diagrams face a concrete, high-cost barrier; this directly targets trust and independent verification.
impact_evidence: Pitch and story identify screen-reader users and verification as the problem.
Workflow screenshot includes branching, blocked, action, and condition states that are difficult to inspect linearly.
creativity_rationale: Using WebMCP as an evidence and verification layer for accessible 2D canvases is a distinctive, socially valuable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Deep-link-to-proof framing goes beyond generic accessible CRUD.
Concept addresses scope/location/completeness verification across complex visual state.
usability_note: The claimed keyboard/screen-reader support and evidence links are promising; assistive behavior is not directly observed.
red_flags: No transcript and static frame evidence cannot confirm screen-reader output or agent calls.
standouts: Impact is unusually clear and tied to an underserved verification need.
advance_reason: High-impact accessibility concept with a meaningful structured-state and proof advantage.

one_line: Buyer and seller agents negotiate a multidimensional deal before human confirmation.
what_it_does: Negotiates price, quantity, freebies, shipping, and coupons through storefront tools, then presents a human-confirmed order.
leverage_rationale: Multi-round negotiation over coupled economic constraints is difficult to reproduce reliably through generic UI driving; shared buyer/seller state and a guarded confirmation are central.
leverage_evidence: About text describes storefront tools for search, details, cart, add-ons, coupons, and negotiation.
One OffersService mutation path enforces buyer budget and seller floor across turns.
execution_rationale: The architecture and product story are unusually concrete, including one mutation path and confirmation gate, though no video was submitted.
execution_evidence: About text specifies Next/React frontend, backend persistence, multi-round negotiation, and explicit economic limits.
Live demo and public repo are reported.
impact_rationale: Shoppers and merchants have a recognizable desire for better deals and reduced negotiation effort; human confirmation mitigates purchase risk.
impact_evidence: Product targets real shopping negotiations involving shipping, coupons, quantity, and add-ons.
Nothing is purchased until the human confirms.
creativity_rationale: A browser agent haggling against a store agent over a full deal, rather than a single price, is novel and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Negotiation spans several coupled deal dimensions and multiple rounds.
Human approval is integrated as a deliberate interaction boundary.
usability_note: Confirmation and constraint enforcement suggest safe usability; actual interaction is not observed.
red_flags: No frame sheets; core negotiation behavior is described rather than visually verified.
standouts: Strongest WebMCP indispensability claim among commerce entries.
advance_reason: Highly differentiated agent interaction with credible safety and state guarantees.

one_line: Text-first Korean navigation for screen-reader users with agent-readable transit tools.
what_it_does: Searches places, returns accessibility and transit details, plans routes, exposes route details, and lets users inspect the same text-first screen.
leverage_rationale: A single structured call aggregates data from multiple public APIs into concise, screen-reader-verifiable answers; generic browser driving would require fragile multi-page traversal.
leverage_evidence: Transcript says one tool returns timetable, facilities, elevators, and live arrivals from four APIs.
Video shows shared route screen and agent-readable text; seven tools are named.
execution_rationale: The 126-second video provides direct evidence of the app, tool registration, route output, truncation strategy, and shared screen, supported by a mature product history.
execution_evidence: Transcript explicitly demonstrates a 3,700-character transit answer compressed into best route plus on-demand details.
Screenshot visibly shows a text-based station page with station info, directions, and accessibility-oriented controls.
impact_rationale: Blind and screen-reader users navigating South Korea have a specific, consequential need for textual transit and accessibility information; the solution directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Creator describes being a blind user and building around real navigation barriers.
Output includes elevators, barrier-free facilities, car/door guidance, and no coordinates/maps.
creativity_rationale: A mapless navigation product designed around plain language and agent/user shared verification is a deeply pursued, memorable alternative to map-centric navigation.
creativity_evidence: WebMCP tools mirror the same sentences that screen-reader users hear and connect into a chain.
usability_note: Text-first output, route detail on demand, and shared screen verification are strong accessibility choices.
red_flags: Core navigation app predates the challenge, though the packet says WebMCP tools were built during submission period.
standouts: Exceptional direct evidence and user-problem fit.
Clear explanation of how WebMCP compresses and structures multi-source transit data.
advance_reason: Outstanding impact, leverage, and evidence quality for an accessibility-first navigation workflow.

one_line: Guided HIPAA-aware AI adoption workspace for medical practices.
what_it_does: Teaches AI boundaries, evaluates clinical workflows, stages a 21-day adoption mission, and requires human approval of policy gates.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools help an agent navigate lessons, workflow assessment, and gated planning in shared state, but much of the experience could be approximated by ordinary form automation.
leverage_evidence: About text lists ten tools for inspecting workspace, focusing lessons, selecting use cases, assessing readiness, staging missions, and approval.
Packaging screenshot is described as showing tools discovered and page changes.
execution_rationale: The scope is coherent and safety-conscious, but no video frames were submitted and the packet gives limited direct evidence of the core flow.
execution_evidence: Public repo and live demo are reported.
About text specifies lessons, realistic workflows, policy gates, and public-site debrief.
impact_rationale: Physicians and practice leaders have a real need for bounded, understandable AI adoption guidance that avoids PHI and preserves clinical judgment.
impact_evidence: Product targets doctors unsure how to use AI within HIPAA.
Synthetic rehearsal, minimum-necessary data, vendor path, and human clinical judgment are explicit boundaries.
creativity_rationale: The combination of adoption education, readiness assessment, and approval-gated mission planning is a fresh application of WebMCP to healthcare operations.
creativity_evidence: 21-day mission and personally approved policy gates create a concrete interaction model.
Public practice-domain debrief deliberately excludes portals, private pages, and PHI.
usability_note: Guided lessons and gates should help a cautious audience, but the actual interface is not visually evidenced here.
red_flags: No frame sheets and limited concrete visual evidence.
Healthcare compliance claims should not be treated as proof of legal compliance.
standouts: Explicitly bounded synthetic/public-data approach and human policy approval.

one_line: Shared screenplay editor where an agent writes directly into the live document.
what_it_does: Maintains story bible, outline, character bible, scenes, ideas, and consistency checks through direct structured document edits.
leverage_rationale: Direct structured edits preserve screenplay formatting, shared context, and consistency across a live document; copy/paste chat workflows lose these properties.
leverage_evidence: About text lists tools for premise, outline, scenes, lines, characters, ideas, ordering, and consistency.
get_script is explicitly intended to ground the agent in the human-authored outline and story bible.
execution_rationale: The product model is coherent and detailed, with a broad screenplay surface, but direct operation is not shown beyond static packaging evidence.
execution_evidence: Story describes act-by-act screenplay formatting and live same-page updates.
Public repo and live demo are reported; frame sheets were submitted but no direct analysis was available.
impact_rationale: Screenwriters and co-writing teams have a real problem maintaining formatting and story context through agent round trips; this directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Product targets screenplay drafting and revision.
Shared story bible and outline grounding reduce continuity drift.
creativity_rationale: Treating the agent as a live screenplay collaborator with structured narrative memory is a strong, focused interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Same-page editing and get_script-first grounding are distinctive design choices.
Idea board, character bible, outline, and consistency tools pursue the concept in depth.

standouts: Strong grounding strategy via an explicit get_script-first tool description.
advance_reason: Clear WebMCP advantage for structured creative writing and a well-specified collaborative document model.

one_line: Approval-gated studio for authoring and rendering fictional coding-agent sessions.
what_it_does: Lets an agent write scripts, direct stage/camera/look, preview and measure timing, render SVG/video, and obtain approval before rewrites or export.
leverage_rationale: The agent can inspect and mutate structured stage state, timeline, and renders directly, while the human sees calls and controls approvals; generic UI driving would be fragile for deterministic media authoring.
leverage_evidence: Transcript shows load script, camera, choice, theme, terminal surface, and export interactions.
About text enumerates tools for timeline inspection, snapshots, duration fitting, proposals, approvals, and export.
execution_rationale: The video transcript gives unusually concrete evidence of a complete authoring session: script creation, rendering, choices, voice input, theme changes, timeline, and export.
execution_evidence: 170-second video transcript reports stage playback, agent call log, approved choice, voice input, direct scene changes, and animated SVG export.
Frame preview visibly shows a coding-agent session with search, explanation, approval, and 14/14 tests passed.
impact_rationale: Developers, educators, and presenters have a real need for re-shootable, secret-free demonstrations of agent sessions; deterministic rendering provides credible value.
impact_evidence: About text targets READMEs, docs, talks, and posts.
Client-only/privacy default avoids leaking secrets and supports repeatable exports.
creativity_rationale: A stage that turns fictional agent interactions into controllable, measurable, multi-surface media is an original and ambitious use of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Agent directs script, camera, timing, themes, choices, and export rather than merely generating text.
Every-word listing, deterministic camera, and approval cards deepen the concept.
usability_note: Approval gates, visible call rail, and deterministic preview support safe creative iteration.
red_flags: Underlying SVGent appears pre-existing; challenge-specific WebMCP binding is the relevant new work.
standouts: Excellent direct product-motion evidence and unusually complete control surface.
Human approval is consistently preserved for rewrites and export.
advance_reason: Highly creative, well-evidenced agent-directed authoring product with strong execution.
